sources.title: Structured interview source containing the matrix longest-increasing-path prompt
Independent exact-candidate matrix longest-increasing-path topological differential validation
Fresh isolated source-first matrix longest-increasing-path review

claims.text: The preserved source asks only for the longest increasing path in a matrix; four-direction movement, strict increase, rectangular input, null/empty handling and Java API behavior are explicit candidate contracts rather than preserved source wording.
The candidate defines memo[r][c] as the longest path starting at the cell and explores only strictly larger four-direction neighbors, allowing each state to be computed once and reused.

Under the explicit strict-increase contract every legal edge increases the value, so the state graph is acyclic; with at most four outgoing neighbor checks per cell, memoized DFS performs O(mn) state work, uses O(mn) memo storage and may use O(mn) recursion depth.

Writer and independent reviewer validations cover deterministic edge cases, empty and jagged-input contracts, 840 exhaustive small matrices and 20000 seeded randomized matrices, with the reviewer using an independent Kahn topological-layer oracle.

validation.command: extract the exact candidate Java block, compile it in an independent harness, and compare deterministic plus 840 exhaustive and 20000 seeded randomized matrices against an independent Kahn topological-layer oracle
validation.reported_stdout: PASS exact_candidate deterministic=7 exhaustive=840 randomized=20000 oracle=kahn-topological-layers strict=greater rectangular=validated empty=0
checks: exact candidate Java implementation compiles under Java 21 inside an independent harness
null, zero-row, zero-column and jagged-array behaviors follow the candidate contract
standard, rectangular, equal-valued, negative-valued, row-only and column-only deterministic cases match expected lengths
840 exhaustive small matrices match an independent Kahn topological-layer oracle
20000 seeded randomized matrices up to 7x7 match the independent Kahn topological-layer oracle
strict greater-than four-direction movement preserves acyclicity and the exact candidate never requires a path-level visited set

findings: The answer preserves the exact matrix-longest-increasing-path source boundary and explicitly labels four-direction movement, strict increase, rectangular input and null/empty behavior as candidate contracts rather than source facts.
The memoized DFS state is coherent: memo[r][c] means the best path starting at the current cell, so each cell is fully expanded once and reused by all predecessors.

Under the explicit strict-increase rule, every legal directed edge increases the cell value, so the state graph is acyclic; the no-path-level-visited explanation is therefore justified for this contract.
The exact candidate Java compiles under Java 21 and independently matches a Kahn topological-layer oracle on deterministic cases, 840 exhaustive small matrices and 20000 seeded randomized matrices.
The answer covers empty input, jagged Java arrays, equal values, negative values, four-versus-eight-direction variation, recursion-depth risk and the alternative iterative topological formulation.

The O(mn) time and O(mn) memo-space claims are consistent with one memoized expansion per cell and at most four neighbor checks per expansion; the answer separately records worst-case O(mn) recursion depth.
No fabricated production experience or result is claimed; the project section remains a clearly hypothetical implementation-choice discussion.
